title: Term Weighting: Visual Guide
outline: 1. From Sets To Scores | four documents and the query `vector database` re-ranked under Boolean AND, sum of raw tf, raw tf x idf and log tf x idf | Boolean intersection returns an unordered set, and each correction changes the winner: raw tf lets D4 win on ten occurrences of the common term, log tf x idf drops it to last

2. The Saturation Curve | a term-frequency slider with landmark stops over raw, sqrt, log and binary transforms, plus the ratio against a document with 8 occurrences | evidence must grow sublinearly: 1, 2, 10, 100 become 1, 1.693, 3.303, 5.605, and the 80-vs-8 spam gap shrinks from 10x under raw tf to 1.75x under log tf

3. Rarity Is Information | document frequency dragged from 0 to 10,000 with the p = df/N, -log p, log(N/df) derivation recomputing live and named terms marked | idf is information content, so df = N gives 0, df = 100 gives exactly twice df = 1,000, df = 0 divides by zero and needs handling before scoring, and maximal rarity can just be a typo

4. Choosing A Scheme | tf and df sliders driving binary, raw, log, augmented and boolean-without-idf weights side by side, with SMART notation in the note | the variants are a family of claims about repetition and rarity: at tf 3 and df 100 raw gives 13.815 and log gives 9.665, and at df = N every idf-bearing scheme collapses to 0 while boolean-no-idf still reports 1

5. Title Boost Crossover | title weight and Y's body repetition dragged against document X (title x1, body x10), with each score split into title and body contributions | a fielded scheme makes title evidence explicit, and because tf is logarithmic the crossover is t* = 10 e^w, so each unit of title weight costs the competitor another factor of e in repetition
